patches.value: u is the unique real mean-zero C([0,T];H^gamma) distributional KdV solution with datum q, v=S_(-t)u satisfies v'=B_t(v,v)/2, and sup||u||_(H^gamma)<=A(T,gamma,R). For smooth q, u is smooth.

For all I=[a,b] with 0<=a<=b and h=b-a<=1, all 0<=sigma<=1 and paths f_j in L^infty(I;H^sigma) with weak derivatives in L^infty(I;H^(-pstar)), Ctri satisfies ||C_I(f1,f2,f3)||_2<=C*h*product_j||f_j||_(X(I))+C*||f_i||_(L^infty H^(-pstar))*product_{j!=i}||f_j||_(L^infty L^2), each i=1,2,3. For time-independent inputs, ||C_I(f1,f2,f3)||_2<=C_sigma*h^sigma*product_j||f_j||_(H^sigma), including sigma=0.
For the fixed tau>0 and arbitrary real alpha,beta, |eta_tau(alpha,beta)|<=tau*min(|alpha|,|beta|), and eta_tau(alpha,beta)=0 if alpha*beta=0.

For polynomial mean-zero inputs and 0<=sigma<=1, ||R2_(a0,tau)(f1,f2,f3)||_2<=C_sigma*tau^(1+sigma)*product_j||fj||_(H^sigma); the same bound holds after any multiplier of modulus <=1 is inserted in its Fourier sum.

For all mean-zero L^2 inputs, ||Dinv f||_(H^1)+||Dinv f||_infinity<=C||f||_2 and ||J_t(f,g)||_(H^1)<=C||f||_2||g||_2. For A,A2 in H^1, ||AA2||_(H^1)<=C||A||_(H^1)||A2||_(H^1). S_t is unitary and strongly continuous on every H^s and preserves reality and mean.

For mean-zero L^2 inputs ||B_t(f,g)||_(H^(-pstar))<=C||f||_2||g||_2; for arbitrary L^2 F,G, ||Dinv P(FG)||_2<=C||F||_2||G||_2. For mean-zero A with Dinv A in L^2, ||A||_(H^(-pstar))<=||Dinv A||_2 and ||J_t(A,g)||_2<=C||Dinv A||_2||g||_2.
Under L1, q<=2, sup||F_n||_(H^1)<=C_M, sup||F_n-F_(t_n)(t;w,w)||_(H^1)<=C_M*delta, sup(||F_n||_(H^a_gamma)+||F_n||_2)<=C_M*q and ||z_n||_X<=C_M.
Under L1, sup||Dinv B_t(f,F_n)||_2<=C_M*q, sup||Dinv Y_n||_2<=C_M*tau*q and sup||Dinv Y_n'||_2<=C_M*q.

For mean-zero f,g in L^2 and all real t, ||Dinv f||_(H^1)+||Dinv f||_infinity<=C||f||_2, ||B_t(f,g)||_(H^(-pstar))<=C||f||_2||g||_2, ||J_t(f,g)||_(H^1)<=C||f||_2||g||_2, and ||Dinv P(fg)||_2<=C||f||_2||g||_2. For mean-zero A, ||A||_(H^(-pstar))<=||Dinv A||_2 whenever the latter is finite; ||J_t(A,g)||_2<=C||Dinv A||_2||g||_2. H^1 is an algebra: ||A*A2||_(H^1)<=C||A||_(H^1)||A2||_(H^1). S_t is unitary in every H^s, preserves reality/mean and is strongly continuous. For piecewise time-smooth spatially smooth mean-zero paths f,g on [a,b], integral_a^b B_t(f,g)dt=(1/3)[J_t(f,g)]_a^b-(1/3)integral_a^b[J_t(f',g)+J_t(f,g')]dt. Also J_t is symmetric and integral_I J_t(B_t(f,g),h)dt=C_I(f,g,h). In particular F_a(t;f,g)=[J_s(f,g)]_(s=a)^(s=t)/6 for constant inputs. All bounded product maps extend from polynomials by density.
